newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: COURT TO HEAR COAL AND ALLIED DISPUTE.
newsitem.headline: COURT TO HEAR COAL AND ALLIED DISPUTE.

text.p: Coal and Allied Industries Ltd (CAIL) and the Construction, Forestry Mining and Energy Union (CFMEU) will appear before the Australian Industrial Relations Commission (AIRC) on Tuesday after failing to resolve their differences in talks on Monday.
The AIRC hearing will begin on Tuesday morning, the parties told Reuters after a day of talks.

"We're not very hopeful of a breakthrough," Paddy Gorman, CFMEU communications officer said. Thirty six issues had been discussed with the CFMEU giving way on 20 but CAIL not having conceded one, he said.
Gorman said a strike has not been called although advance notification had been given of the existence of a dispute.
"We're quite happy to negotiate a settlement to the dispute but we don't think the company wants to negotiate seriously."
A spokesman for CAIL said progress was being made in talks with the CFMEU over a collective agreement.
"We have offered to continue negotiations for another month if they don't go on strike. They have yet to withdraw their notice of strike," he said.
The company spokesman said the next step was a report expected back from the AIRC by mid-Tueday.

The dispute is at CAIL's Hunter Valley No 1 mine north of Sydney. The mine normally produces about 25,000 tonnes of semi-soft coking coal and thermal coal a day for export to Japanese and other east Asian power stations, steel mills and industrial customers.
Members of the CFMEU last returned to work on July 22 after a bitter six week strike at the mine which CAIL said cost the company A$1 million each day in lost sales revenue.
CAIL is owned about 70 percent by mining giant Rio Tinto Ltd.
